author: khanhtranngoccva
body:
This method aims to solve issue #86 by ensuring every inode has at least one chance to have a stable backing ID, as well as making a few major modifications on the hybrid ID to allow for trivial ID creation (to pass into prune(), make it easier to unit test, and separate code concerns).

Here are the changes:
1. Create a `setup` method that runs pre-mount to allow the implementations to store the `TResolver` types.
2. Create a `lookup_root` method that runs pre-mount to allow the implementations to return a proper backing ID for the root inode. Currently, if the method is not implemented (ENOSYS), the bootstrapper that runs the code only warns the user.
3. For the theoretical ease of unit testing, `HybridId` no longer has the convenience methods. It is instead moved inside the resolver types, which also allows separation of concerns. It also makes sense, because the `HybridId`'s internal inode might become invalid through a forget() call when the struct is still in scope.

I'm also considering that the inode resolver APIs should return an error at `inode_mapping` level since the user can now pass invalid inodes.

author: nagariahussain
body:
## Summary
- `apply_merge_revision` builds its `key_to_name` map only from documents within the space's nested set range (`lft`/`rgt`). If a Wiki Document with a given `doc_key` exists outside that range (e.g. orphaned after a tree rebuild or a prior failed merge), the code would attempt to insert a new document, hitting the unique constraint on `doc_key` and raising `UniqueValidationError`.
- Added a global lookup for existing documents with the same `doc_key` before creating a new one. If found, the existing document is loaded and updated (re-parented into the space) instead of inserting a duplicate.

## Test plan
- [ ] Reproduce by having a Wiki Document with a `doc_key` that exists in the DB but falls outside the space's nested set tree, then merge a change request referencing that `doc_key`
- [ ] Verify the merge completes without `UniqueValidationError`
- [ ] Verify the document is correctly re-parented into the space after merge

author: fanyang89

### Motivation

- Improve throughput by decoupling JSON parsing from DuckDB writes so parsing can proceed while writes complete, reducing idle IO waiting.

### Description

- Introduced a buffered `events` channel and a writer goroutine that consumes events and calls `appender.AppendRow` in `cmd_vfs_raw.go`.
- Added a `writeErrCh` to propagate writer errors back to the parser and a `done` channel to coordinate shutdown.
- Changed the `jsonParseThenAppend` callback to send parsed `*vfsEvent` into the `events` channel and handle early writer errors.
- Ensured orderly shutdown by closing `events`, waiting for the writer to finish, and returning any parse or write errors.

author: fanyang89
body:
### Motivation

- Reduce per-event allocations when parsing bpftrace NDJSON/logfmt output by reusing event structs. 
- Improve performance and GC pressure for high-throughput `printf` event streams.

### Description

- Add a `sync.Pool` for raw event types and import `sync` in `cmd_net.go`, `cmd_proc.go`, `cmd_mem.go`, `cmd_syscall.go`, and `cmd_vfs_raw.go`.
- Reset pooled instances before parsing with `*e = <Type>{}` and unmarshal into the pooled object (e.g. `logfmt.Unmarshal(buf, e)`).
- Return pooled objects to the pool on both success and failure paths to avoid leaks, and call `appendRow` with the pooled pointer (e.g. `err = appendRow(e)`).
- Updated parsing functions: `netJSONParseThenAppend`, `procJSONParseThenAppend`, `memJSONParseThenAppend`, `syscallJSONParseThenAppend`, and both parse paths in `cmd_vfs_raw.go` to use the pools.

### Testing

- Files were formatted with `gofmt -w` to ensure idiomatic formatting.
- No automated unit tests were executed as part of this change.

author: yazcaleb
body:
## Summary
- Add first-party integration adapters for browser-use, Playwright, and Puppeteer with shared `BrowserAgentAdapter` interface
- Each adapter validates browser actions (navigate, click, fill, type, etc.) through Veto's validation pipeline before execution
- Include bundled starter policy templates for browser-safe navigation, input, and downloads

## What changed

### New modules (`packages/sdk/src/integrations/`)
- `types.ts` - BrowserAction, NavigationAction, ClickAction, InputAction, DownloadAction type definitions
- `adapter.ts` - `BaseBrowserAdapter` base class with `intercept()` and `wrap()` API, `BrowserActionDeniedError`
- `browser-use.ts` - `BrowserUseAdapter` wrapping browser-use's `act()` method with policy validation
- `playwright.ts` - `PlaywrightAdapter` wrapping `page.goto/click/fill/type/selectOption/evaluate/screenshot`
- `puppeteer.ts` - `PuppeteerAdapter` wrapping `page.goto/click/type/select/evaluate/screenshot`
- `index.ts` - Re-exports all adapters and types

### Starter policies (`packages/sdk/templates/browser/`)
- `browser-safe-navigation.yaml` - Block data:/javascript:/file: URLs, internal networks, known phishing TLDs
- `browser-safe-input.yaml` - Block password/credit card/SSN field filling and sensitive value patterns
- `browser-safe-downloads.yaml` - Block executable/archive downloads, allow safe document formats

### Examples
- `examples/browser-use-example/` - Minimal browser-use + Veto setup with navigation policy
- `examples/playwright-example/` - Playwright + Veto setup with adapter usage patterns

### Package exports
- `veto-sdk/integrations` - All adapters and types
- `veto-sdk/integrations/browser-use` - browser-use adapter only
- `veto-sdk/integrations/playwright` - Playwright adapter only
- `veto-sdk/integrations/puppeteer` - Puppeteer adapter only

## Usage

```typescript
// browser-use: one-line setup
import { wrapBrowserUse } from 'veto-sdk/integrations/browser-use';
const adapter = wrapBrowserUse(veto);
adapter.wrap(tools); // wraps act() with validation

// Playwright: one-line setup
import { wrapPlaywrightPage } from 'veto-sdk/integrations/playwright';
const safePage = wrapPlaywrightPage(veto, page);
await safePage.goto('https://example.com'); // validated

// Puppeteer: one-line setup
import { wrapPuppeteerPage } from 'veto-sdk/integrations/puppeteer';
const safePage = wrapPuppeteerPage(veto, page);
await safePage.goto('https://example.com'); // validated
```

## Test plan
- [x] 52 new tests across 5 test files
- [x] Adapter wrapping validates actions through Veto pipeline
- [x] Denied actions throw `BrowserActionDeniedError` in strict mode

### Motivation

body:
## Summary

Centralizes 12+ hardcoded timeouts, thresholds, and magic numbers from 5 packages into the existing "$(TownSettings)" config system ("$(settings/config.json)"). All changes are additive and backward-compatible — existing config files without new fields continue to work via sensible defaults.

### What changed
- **3 new config structs** added to "$(TownSettings)": "$(WebTimeoutsConfig)" (6 timeout fields), "$(WorkerStatusConfig)" (stale/stuck thresholds), "$(FeedCuratorConfig)" (dedup window, aggregation window, min count)
- **"$(ParseDurationOrDefault)" helper** for safe duration string parsing with automatic fallback
- **12+ hardcoded constants removed** across "$(web/fetcher.go)", "$(web/handler.go)", "$(web/api.go)", "$(feed/curator.go)", and "$(cmd/dashboard.go)" — replaced with config-driven values
- **TUI magic numbers extracted** to named constants ("$(treePanelPercent)", "$(convoyPanelPercent)", "$(maxEventHistory)") — layout details, not user config
- **Bug fix**: "$(MinAggregateCount)" zero-value guard — when "$(FeedCuratorConfig)" is present but "$(min_aggregate_count)" is omitted, JSON unmarshal gives "$(0)", causing every sling event to be incorrectly aggregated. Fixed by falling back to default "$(3)" when "$(<= 0)".

## File-by-file changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| "$(config/types.go)" | +3 config structs, "$(Default*())" constructors, "$(ParseDurationOrDefault)", 3 new pointer fields on "$(TownSettings)" |
| "$(feed/curator.go)" | Loads "$(FeedCuratorConfig)"; removes dead "$(mailAggregateWindow)"; adds zero-value guard for "$(MinAggregateCount)" |
| "$(web/fetcher.go)" | Converts "$(runBdCmd)" to "$(LiveConvoyFetcher)" method; adds timeout/threshold fields; "$(calculateWorkerWorkStatus)" accepts threshold params |
| "$(web/handler.go)" | "$(NewConvoyHandler)" accepts "$(fetchTimeout)"; "$(NewDashboardMux)" accepts "$(*WebTimeoutsConfig)" (nil-safe with defaults) |
| "$(web/api.go)" | "$(NewAPIHandler)" accepts "$(defaultRunTimeout, maxRunTimeout)"; removes hardcoded consts |
| "$(cmd/dashboard.go)" | Loads "$(TownSettings)", threads "$(WebTimeouts)" to "$(NewDashboardMux)"; warns on config load failure |
| "$(tui/feed/model.go)" | Extracts panel layout constants: "$(treePanelPercent=30)", "$(convoyPanelPercent=25)", "$(maxEventHistory=1000)" |
| Test files (6) | +32 new tests; all call sites updated for new constructor signatures |

author: canbal
body:
## Why
The temperature-dependent thermocouple correction introduced in 5d8191e was added to address suspected overfiring due to thermocouple drift.

We’ve since confirmed the overfiring behavior was caused by an aging kiln (unable to climb fast enough), leading to excessive heatwork/overexposure that should be addressed by lowering firing temps (or replacing elements), not by correcting the thermocouple reading.

## What changed
- Removes `thermocouple_correction_table` usage and the helper interpolation logic.
- Restores the previous behavior that uses `config.thermocouple_offset` directly.

## Files
- `config.py`
- `lib/oven.py`
- `kiln-tuner.py`

### Motivation
- Provide an interactive tool to detect diameters of concentric black circles printed on a white mirror target for manual tuning and measurement.
- Enable ROI cropping to reduce external noise and expose Hough/ preprocessing parameters so operators can stabilize detection across a range of images.

### Description
- Add new script `kiem_guong.py` implementing a detection pipeline that uses `cv2.HoughCircles` and a `CircleResult` dataclass with concentric filtering by median center using `center_tol` and radius deduplication using `min_radius_gap`.
- Provide an OpenCV interactive UI with trackbars for crop margins (`crop_left_px`, `crop_right_px`, `crop_top_px`, `crop_bottom_px`), blur (`blur_ksize`), Hough-related parameters (`hough_dp_x10`, `minDist`, `canny_param1`, `acc_param2`, `minRadius`, `maxRadius`) and tuning controls (`center_tol`, `min_radius_gap`).
- Annotate and display results on the image and ROI grayscale view, show number of circles and diameters in pixels on-screen, and support saving the annotated result via `s` and exiting via `q`.

### Testing
- Ran `python -m py_compile kiem_guong.py` which succeeded.
- Attempting to run the app (`python kiem_guong.py --help`) in this environment failed due to a missing system library (`libGL.so.1`) that prevented `cv2` GUI initialization, so interactive runtime validation was not executed.

body:
Match rule files to corresponding targets when config and test directories differ, mirroring semgrep test pairing logic.

Before: if you ran `opengrep test --config tests/rules/ tests/targets/`, the `Test_CLI.Dir (_, Some config_str)` branch would hit a failwith that said split rules/targets weren’t supported yet.

After: when `--config` points to a directory, it now:
- collects rule files from the rules dir (`Rule_tests.get_config_filenames`),
- pairs each rule file with matching target files in the targets dir (`Rule_tests.get_config_test_filenames`),
- filters out rules with no targets (warns + records MissingTest),
- logs which targets were found and returns `(rule_file, targets)` pairs.

author: jlieow
body:
## Changes
The `databricks_sql_table` resource times out with custom `warehouse_id` when SQL tables take longer than 50 seconds to create and Terraform does not record it in state. On the next `terraform apply`, Terraform tries to create the table again but fails because it already exists, leaving the user stuck and having to import the resource into the state.                                                

This issue is not present when the `warehouse_id` is excluded. When you provide a `warehouse_id`, it routes to the SQL Statement Execution API which uses a SQL Warehouse and has a timeout limit of 50s. When you exclude it, it is sent to a completely different Command Execution API which uses a Cluster and does not have any timeout upper limit, resulting in a different user experience.

Ideally the experience should be the same regardless of the chosen compute. However, the SQL Statement Execution API has a `wait_timeout` parameter that controls how long the API waits before responding, with a maximum of 50 seconds. It also has an `on_wait_timeout` parameter with two options:
- **Cancel**: The statement is aborted after the timeout. However, the table may still end up being created on the Databricks side. Since Terraform saw an error, it never records the table in its state file.
- **Continue**: The statement keeps running after the timeout, but the API returns without a final result. The table is eventually created on the Databricks side, but Terraform still has no success response to record in state.

Users requested adding a Terraform `timeouts` block. However, this does not fully solve the issue either. If a user sets a timeout that is too short for their table to be created, the same problem occurs. The provider gives up waiting, never records the table in state, but the table may still be created on the Databricks side. This puts the burden on the user to guess the right timeout value, and getting it wrong leads to the same stuck state.

The most reliable fix is to use `Continue` instead of `Cancel` (which keeps the statement running after the timeout) and then poll a separate API (`GetStatementByStatementId`) internally to check the statement's progress until it completes. By always waiting for a definitive result (either success or failure), the provider ensures the table is recorded in state when it is created, and future `terraform apply` runs work seamlessly without manual intervention. This also aligns the user experience for both compute types and means no changes to the resource block structure are required.

The `Continue` behavior is applied for all users rather than making it optional because providing a choice would risk users leaving the default as `Cancel` or choosing `Cancel` explicitly, which would still result in tables not being added to state when they take longer than 50 seconds to create. 
  
## Tests
Added `TestResourceSqlTableCreateTable_ExistingSQLWarehouse_Polling` to verify polling behavior when statements take longer than the initial 50-second wait period.

- [x] `make test` run locally
- [ ] relevant change in `docs/` folder
- [x] covered with integration tests in `catalog/resource_sql_table_test.go`
- [x] using Go SDK
- [ ] using TF Plugin Framework
- [x] has entry in `NEXT_CHANGELOG.md` file

No changes to the terraform block is made, just an alignment of user experience, so no update to docs is required. 

The changes are made to SDKv2 as this update is too big to also include a migration to the Plugin Framework.

Fixes #5340

## Fix minifier incorrectly handling `+[false]` and `+[true]`

- [x] Explore repository structure and locate the bug
- [x] Identify the root cause in `to_number` implementation for arrays
- [x] Add test case for the bug in minifier fold_constants tests
- [x] Add test case in to_number unit tests
- [x] Fix the bug in `to_number.rs` to properly convert arrays to strings first
- [x] Run tests to verify the fix - all tests passing
- [x] Manual verification with minifier example - outputs NaN correctly
- [x] Run code review - no issues found
- [x] Run security check - no vulnerabilities found
- [x] Comprehensive testing of all array conversion cases - all correct
- [x] Apply cargo fmt to fix formatting
- [x] Address PR feedback: hoist use statements, simplify comments and code
- [x] Address bot feedback: optimize count, remove redundant import, add test coverage

**Summary:**
Fixed a bug where `+[false]` and `+[true]` were incorrectly minified to `0` and `1` instead of `NaN`. The issue was in the `to_number` implementation for arrays in `oxc_ecmascript`, which was bypassing the proper ECMAScript conversion chain (array → string → number). Now correctly converts arrays to strings first via `to_js_string`, then converts the string to a number.

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

>

> *This section details on the original issue you should resolve*
> 
> <issue_title>minifier: `+[false]` and `+[true]` are incorrectly minified</issue_title>

> I was messing around with [jsfuck](https://jsfuck.com/) and found out that oxc_minifier doesn't minify `+[false]` or `+[true]` correctly. It is supposed to evalutate to `NaN`, but Oxc just grabs the boolean and uses that. This makes the 'minified' jsfuck code invalid (not that I'm using jsfuck on a day to day basis)
> 
> Original:
> ```ts
> const a = +[false]
> const b = +[true]
> ```
> 
> Oxc minified:
> ```ts
> const a = 0
> const b = 1;
> ```
> 
> Expected:
> ```ts
> const a = NaN
> const b = NaN;
> ```
>

>

author: pracucci
body: #### What this PR does In this PR I'm adding the `MimirCompactorOOMKilled` alert. Contrary to other Mimir components, when a compactor OOM it's very likely that will continue to OOM until we give it more memory. Why? Because if a compactor OOMs when processing a compaction job, that same compaction job will retried over and over. Today we don't have any alert firing when a compactor OOMs continuously. In this PR I'm proposing a new alert, both warning and critical severity. I've backtested the alert at Grafana Labs (last 30d) and it would have always fired when there was a real issue, and compactor memory should have been increased (left side = warning query, right side = critical query): #### Which issue(s) this PR fixes or relates to N/A #### Checklist - [ ] Tests updated. - [ ] Documentation added. - [x] `CHANGELOG.md` updated - the order of entries should be `[CHANGE]`, `[FEATURE]`, `[ENHANCEMENT]`, `[BUGFIX]`. body:
## Summary
Refactored the Stripe checkout session metadata handling to improve data consistency and ensure location/shipping information is available at the payment intent level.

## Key Changes
- Extracted bounds array destructuring and metadata object creation into a reusable `orderMetadata` variable
- Converted bounds coordinates from array format to individual named fields (`top_left_lat`, `top_left_lng`, `bottom_right_lat`, `bottom_right_lng`) for better clarity and accessibility
- Added `payment_intent_data.metadata` to the checkout session configuration, ensuring order metadata is attached to the payment intent in addition to the session
- Removed `JSON.stringify()` call on bounds, replacing it with explicit coordinate fields

## Implementation Details
- The bounds array is destructured as `[south, west, north, east]` following the standard geographic bounds convention
- All coordinate values are converted to strings for consistent metadata storage
- The same `orderMetadata` object is now used for both session and payment intent metadata, ensuring data consistency across Stripe objects
- This change enables better access to location and shipping information when processing payments and webhooks

author: qu0b
body:
## Summary

- Adds `eip2780tx` scenario with 8 modes that exercise EIP-2780 granular gas accounting paths
- Includes `EIP2780Helper.sol` contract with `nop()`, `forwardValue()`, and `createAndDestroy()` functions
- Registered in the "Simple" scenario category

### Modes

| Mode | EIP-2780 Gas Path | Description |
|---|---|---|
| `new-account` | GAS_NEW_ACCOUNT surcharge | Value transfer to random fresh address |
| `precompile` | Precompile warmth rules | Value transfer to 0x01-0x09 (cycling) |
| `access-list` | WARM vs COLD recipient | Value transfer with recipient in access list |
| `contract-call` | COLD_ACCOUNT_COST_CODE | Call deployed contract's `nop()` |
| `value-call` | CALL_VALUE_COST | Contract forwards ETH to existing EOA |
| `value-call-new` | CALL_VALUE_COST + GAS_NEW_ACCOUNT | Contract forwards ETH to fresh address |
| `selfdestruct` | EIP-6780 create+destroy | Create child + selfdestruct in same tx |
| `all` (default) | All above | Cycles through all modes round-robin |

## Test plan

- [x] `go fmt`, `go vet` pass
- [x] `go build -tags=with_blob_v1,ckzg ./cmd/...` succeeds
- [x] `spamoor eip2780tx --help` shows all flags including `--mode`
- [x] Tested in kurtosis ethereum-package (geth+lighthouse, minimal preset) - contract deployed, all 7 modes cycling with 100% tx confirmation rate over 18+ blocks

author: boujonlaurin-dotcom
body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
This pull request completes Phase 3: Polish, significantly enhancing the digest feature with new user-facing functionalities, improved data insights, increased reliability, and performance optimizations.

Key changes include:

*   **Daily Local Push Notifications**: Implemented a `PushNotificationService` to send daily local push notifications at 8 AM (Europe/Paris) to inform users that their digest is ready. This includes opt-out functionality in settings, notification permission requests for Android 13+, and navigation directly to the Digest Screen upon tapping the notification.
*   **Unified Content Analytics**:
    *   Introduced a unified `content_interaction` event type for all content actions (read, save, dismiss, pass) across both feed and digest surfaces, replacing fragmented event tracking.
    *   Added surface-specific `digest_session` and `feed_session` events to capture session-level engagement.
    *   The analytics schema now includes a nullable `atomic_themes` field for forward-compatibility with future content enrichment.
    *   Extended both backend and mobile `AnalyticsService` with unified tracking methods, deprecating older, fragmented methods.
*   **Digest Metrics Endpoint**: A new backend endpoint (`GET /api/analytics/digest-metrics`) was added to provide key performance indicators for digest engagement, such as completion rate, average closure time, and a breakdown of user actions (read, save, dismiss, pass) over a specified period. This endpoint uses optimized SQL queries for JSONB aggregation.
*   **Comprehensive Unit Tests**: Added 24 new unit tests for the `DigestSelector` and `DigestService` components. These tests cover the digest selection algorithm's logic (e.g., selection count, source diversity, decay factor, 4-tuple return, edge cases) and the service's action handling (read, save, not_interested, undo) and completion logic, serving as a robust regression safety net.
*   **Performance Optimization**:
    *   **Backend N+1 Query Elimination**: Optimized digest retrieval in `DigestService` by batch-fetching all content items and their associated user action states using `selectinload` and `IN` queries, reducing the number of database queries from 2*N (where N is the number of digest items) to a fixed 3 queries.
    *   **Structured Logging with Timing**: Replaced standard logging with `structlog` in the digest API router and added `elapsed_ms` timing to all digest-related endpoints for improved performance monitoring and debugging.
    *   **Client-Side In-Memory Caching**: Implemented in-memory caching for the daily digest within the mobile `DigestNotifier` provider. This prevents redundant API calls when users navigate away from and back to the digest screen within the same day, with optimistic updates on user actions and a `forceRefresh()` option.

This comprehensive update significantly improves the user experience, provides richer and more consistent data for future recommendation system tuning, and enhances the overall stability and efficiency of the digest system.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

## Summary
This PR adds wallet adapter support to the Aptree SDK by introducing `*Payload` methods across all builder classes. These methods generate `InputEntryFunctionData` objects that can be passed directly to wallet adapters' `signAndSubmitTransaction` without requiring network calls.

## Key Changes

- **New `buildPayload` method in `BaseModule`**: A protected helper that creates `InputEntryFunctionData` objects from function identifiers and arguments, complementing the existing `buildTransaction` method
- **Payload methods for all builders**: Added corresponding `*Payload` methods for every transaction-building method in:
  - `BridgeBuilder` (6 payload methods)
  - `LockingBuilder` (7 payload methods)
  - `GuaranteedYieldBuilder` (12 payload methods)
  - `MockVaultBuilder` (8 payload methods)
  - `GladeBuilder` (6 payload methods)
- **Re-exported `InputEntryFunctionData`**: Made the Aptos SDK type available to consumers via the main SDK export
- **Version bump**: Updated package version from 0.1.2 to 0.2.0

## Implementation Details

- Payload methods follow the same argument structure as their transaction counterparts but skip network calls
- Each payload method is documented with JSDoc comments linking to the corresponding transaction method
- The implementation maintains consistency across all builders by using the shared `buildPayload` helper
- Type safety is preserved with proper TypeScript definitions in both `.d.ts` and `.d.mts` files

body:
Mobile app had no visual feedback during background operations (repository loading, cloning, rollback, etc.), leaving users uncertain whether actions were processing.

## Changes

**Added global loading overlay**
- Full-screen semi-transparent backdrop with blur effect
- Animated spinner with contextual status messages
- Reference-counted visibility for nested async operations

**Integration points**
- Repository operations: load, refresh, validate
- GitHub operations: auth, clone, list repos
- Workspace operations: initialize, cleanup
- Git operations: rollback, timeline fetch

**Implementation**
```javascript
// Show loading with custom messages
showGlobalLoading('Cloning repository...', 'This may take a few minutes');

// Auto-hides when operation completes
hideGlobalLoading();

// Reference counting handles concurrent operations
showGlobalLoading('Loading...', 'Please wait');  // count: 1, shows overlay
showGlobalLoading('Syncing...', 'Please wait');  // count: 2, overlay stays
hideGlobalLoading();  // count: 1, overlay stays
hideGlobalLoading();  // count: 0, overlay hides
```

**Cleanup**
- Removed redundant local spinners that created duplicate feedback

author: turdjali
body:
### Motivation
- Make Replay cameras and cue animations match the live shot (skip the player starting camera, shorten pocket-camera hold and align cue-stroke timing). 
- Prevent balls escaping the playfield and make on-table motion feel more natural. 
- Improve ball-in-hand UX so users can press-hold-and-drag more responsively and show the hand icon consistently when placement is available. 
- Raise AI quality by improving candidate selection, lookahead, sampling and safety/risk handling.

### Description
- Replay and camera: enabled table mapping overlay (`ENABLE_TABLE_MAPPING_LINES = true`) and added `REPLAY_CAMERA_START_DELAY_MS` so recorded replay frames omit the pre-shot player camera snapshot, plus `REPLAY_POCKET_CAMERA_HOLD_MS` and per-playback `pocketCameraCutoff` logic to make pocket camera switches expire earlier during playback; the recorder now conditionally records camera snapshots only after the configured start delay (`recordReplayFrame`). (file: `PoolRoyale.jsx`)
- Cue stroke & timing: reduced replay cue-stroke slowdown (`REPLAY_CUE_STROKE_SLOWDOWN = 1`) so replay cue animation matches live timing and playback behavior. (file: `PoolRoyale.jsx`)
- Ball physics: added a small rolling resistance constant (`ROLLING_RESISTANCE`) and applied a per-substep deceleration when balls are rolling (no lift) to make ball motion feel more natural and reduce drift off-playfield. (file: `PoolRoyale.jsx`)
- Ball-in-hand UX: increased `IN_HAND_DRAG_SPEED` to make press-hold-and-drag faster, show the hand icon whenever `hud.inHand` is active (regardless of turn) and gate pointer drag with a `canDragInHandIcon` flag so the icon is interactive only when player controls permit; updated in-hand icon button attributes and behaviour for pointer capture and drag. (file: `PoolRoyale.jsx`)
- Replay pocket-camera behaviour: store a per-playback `pocketCameraCutoff` and during replay playback, if the camera frames are pocket-camera keyed, hold the pocket view for `REPLAY_POCKET_CAMERA_HOLD_MS` then allow the usual camera transition logic to resume. (file: `PoolRoyale.jsx`)
- AI improvements (open-source planner used): increased planning fidelity by raising `LOOKAHEAD_DEPTH`, `LOOKAHEAD_CANDIDATES`, and `MONTE_CARLO_BASE_SAMPLES`; added `parseBallOnIds` and made `chooseTargets` prefer explicit ball-on ids when present; clamped and passed cue-after predictions into lookahead (`clampPointToTable`) and increased risk margin when evaluating cue-after positions; broadened power & spin sampling for `planShot`. Also pass `ballOn` context into the AI input state from `PoolRoyale.jsx`. (file: `webapp/public/lib/poolAi.js`, `PoolRoyale.jsx`)
- Minor housekeeping: added new constants `REPLAY_CAMERA_START_DELAY_MS`, `REPLAY_POCKET_CAMERA_HOLD_MS`, `ROLLING_RESISTANCE`, and wired them into existing replay/physics logic; small UI tweaks to the in-hand icon (disabled state and opacity). (file: `PoolRoyale.jsx`)

### Testing
- Automated tests: none executed for this patch (no CI/test run performed in this change set).
- Local validation performed: code edits were applied and committed; further automated lint/build/test runs are recommended on CI before merging.

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a deterministic governance layer for benchmarks that enforces runtime and memory budgets and gates performance regressions with deterministic summaries for CI.
- Integrate with existing baseline comparison utilities to detect regressions and produce byte-stable digests for auditability.

### Description
- Add `benchmark_governance.py`: a typed, dataclass-driven governance runner that executes benchmark commands, measures runtime and RSS delta, enforces `BudgetThresholds`, compares runs against stored baselines via `regression_baselines.compare_metrics`, and writes a deterministic `summary` with a `digest` computed by `stable_hash`.
- Add `benchmark_benchmark_governance.py`: a lightweight benchmark script to measure governance-runner overhead using noop Python commands and produce a deterministic digest for the run.
- Add tests `tests/test_benchmark_governance.py` covering budget exceedance and baseline regression detection, and update roadmap/readiness documents `tasks.md` and `AGENTS.md` to mark benchmark governance as Complete.
- Config parsing and validation include `load_governance_config`, `_parse_budgets`, `_parse_thresholds`, and deterministic `config_hash` via `hash_config_path` for reproducible artifacts.

### Testing
- Ran the new governance unit tests with `pytest -q tests/test_benchmark_governance.py`, which passed: `2 passed`.
- The new governance runner was exercised by the test suite to validate budget enforcement, baseline writing, and regression detection.

author: nrminor
body:
## Why a separate PR for the schema version?

The v2.4.0 params schema was released alongside the v2.4.0 tag and is now immutable — users in the wild may be referencing it by URL in their params files for reproducibility. Any new pipeline parameters (from deacon integration, GOTTCHA2, etc.) need to land in a new schema version rather than retroactively modifying v2.4.0.

By putting the version bump in its own PR, we avoid the situation where every feature branch that adds params has to independently create the v2.5.0 file. Instead, this PR establishes v2.5.0 as the open development schema, and feature branches simply add their properties to it.

## What changed

This PR creates `nvd-params.v2.5.0.schema.json` as an identical copy of the released v2.4.0 schema with only the `$id` field updated. It also points the `latest` symlink and the `SCHEMA_URL` in `params.py` at the new version. The v2.4.0 file is untouched.

## Working with this in feature branches

If your feature branch adds new pipeline parameters, it should be based on top of this commit so that it can add properties to the v2.5.0 schema file.

**With jujutsu:** If you created your branch off `main` before this landed, rebase onto the `schema-v2.5.0` bookmark (or onto `main` after this merges):

```
jj rebase -s <your-branch-root> -d schema-v2.5.0
```

To start a new feature branch that depends on this one:

```
jj new schema-v2.5.0 -m "my new feature"
```

**With git:** If your branch predates this change, rebase onto the `schema-v2.5.0` branch (or onto `main` after this merges):

```
git fetch origin
git rebase origin/schema-v2.5.0
```

To start a new feature branch from it:

```
git checkout -b my-feature origin/schema-v2.5.0
```

## Related

This is a dependency of #14 (deacon integration).

### Motivation
- Provide an explicit, reviewable architecture plan that must be approved before any schema, migration, or data-contract changes for settings persistence and enforcement are implemented.
- Prevent accidental behaviour drift by defining ownership, precedence, and server-side enforcement rules up front for workspace vs user settings.
- Reduce rollout and compatibility risk by specifying a migration strategy, dual-read compatibility window, observability needs, and phased rollout gates.

### Description
- Add `docs/settings/persistence-enforcement-architecture-plan.md` that defines the ownership model (workspace-level vs user-level), precedence rules, and target read/write contracts including a typed `resolvedSettings` response shape.
- Classify settings into `display-only` and `enforcement-critical` categories and mandate server-side evaluation/auditing/versioning for enforcement-critical keys (e.g., rules/conflict policy, AI policy, budget thresholds).
- Outline a migration/backfill approach with discovery, mapping, dual-read compatibility, write cutover, and legacy retirement, plus mitigation strategies and a phased rollout (Phase 0..5).
- Add an explicit approval gate listing required approvers and deliverables that must be completed before any schema or data-contract implementation proceeds.

author: gdszyy
body:
## 关联 Issue

Closes #116

## 变更概述

本 PR 实现 Issue #116 中定义的四项性能优化任务：

### 1. 敌人对象池完全支持 (`pool_manager.gd`)

- **池配置扩展**：新增所有敌人类型的池配置（基础五种 + 13 个章节特色 + 8 个精英），每种类型独立配置 `initial/max/expand` 参数
- **章节预热机制**：`warmup_chapter(chapter_index)` 在章节切换时预分配该章节敌人的池，消除运行时首次分配延迟
- **动态池注册**：`register_enemy_pool(type_name, scene)` 支持运行时按需创建新敌人类型的池
- **Shader 预编译**：`_precompile_shaders()` 在启动时通过屏幕外渲染预编译 11 个核心 Shader，防止首次使用时的编译卡顿
- **统计接口**：`get_enemy_pool_summary()` 和 `get_performance_summary()` 提供完整的池状态监控数据
- **章节池释放**：`release_chapter_pools(chapter_index)` 在章节结束时释放不再需要的池内存

### 2. enemy_spawner.gd 对象池完全集成

- **统一获取策略**：所有敌人类型（基础、章节特色、精英）优先通过对象池获取，池未命中时回退到 `instantiate()`
- **统一回收策略**：敌人死亡后通过 `_return_dead_enemy_to_pool()` 归还对象池，不再 `queue_free()`
- **自动注册**：首次遇到未池化的敌人类型时自动调用 `register_enemy_pool()` 创建池
- **预热集成**：章节切换时自动调用 `warmup_chapter()`
- **命中率统计**：`get_pool_hit_rate()` 监控对象池命中率

### 3. 性能基准测试场景 (`performance_benchmark.gd`)

四种测试模式（F1-F4 切换）：

| 测试 | 内容 | 验证目标 |
|------|------|---------|
| F1 弹体压力 | 2000+ 弹体 MultiMesh 渲染 | 60 FPS 目标 |
| F2 对象池吞吐 | acquire/release 循环 | 延迟 < 1ms |
| F3 碰撞压力 | 2000p × 120e 空间哈希 | 碰撞检测 < 2ms/帧 |
| F4 综合压力 | 弹体 + 碰撞 + 对象池 | 综合 60 FPS |

统计指标：平均 FPS、最小 FPS、1% Low FPS、帧时间标准差、碰撞检测耗时、对象池延迟。

author: quaesitor-scientiam
body:
## Summary
- **Return type fallback**: Non-void functions (have `return value` statements) without Python type annotations now get `Any` as the return type instead of omitting it, which caused V compile errors ("Too many return values, expected 0 got 1")
- **Built-in type name escaping**: Python parameters/variables named `string`, `int`, `bool`, `f64`, etc. are now escaped with `@` prefix in V output (`@string`, `@int`) since these conflict with V built-in type names. Type cast usage (e.g. `int(x)`) remains unescaped.
- **Dict type inference**: Improved `infer_expr_type` for `Dict` — falls back to `map[string]Any` when value types can't be inferred, instead of returning empty (which led to missing return types)
- **Cross-platform test runner**: V test runner (`tests/run_tests.v`) now normalizes through `v fmt` and handles `\r\n` line endings, matching the PowerShell runner behavior. Also finds `py2v.exe` on Windows.

## Test plan
- [x] All 100 tests pass on Windows (PowerShell runner)
- [x] All 100 tests pass on WSL Ubuntu (V test runner)
- [x] Verified fix against `selenium/webdriver/common/proxy.py` — `string` parameter properly escaped, `map[string]Any` return type inferred

author: junaway
body: # Azure LiteLLM: Retry Once On Connection Error ## Context We saw intermittent failures when calling Azure OpenAI through LiteLLM. The surfaced error is typically `litellm.APIConnectionError` (AzureException) and may include `RuntimeError: Cannot send a request, as the client has been closed.` in the exception chain. PR `#3539` already added a targeted retry-once for the "http client closed" race by flushing LiteLLM's cached clients and retrying. This change extends that hotpatch to also retry once for Azure calls that fail with `APIConnectionError`, since the underlying "client closed" marker is not always preserved for Azure. ## What Changed File: `sdk/agenta/sdk/litellm/mockllm.py` 1. Centralized retry policy in `_should_retry_litellm_call(...)` to keep `acompletion()` readable. 2. Added Azure detection (`model` starting with `azure/`, or an Azure base URL containing `.openai.azure.com`). 3. Added a retry-once path for Azure `APIConnectionError` (LiteLLM-mapped or OpenAI). 4. Added a tiny jittered sleep (about 100ms) before retrying `azure_api_connection_error` to reduce immediate re-failure. 5. Still flushes LiteLLM's in-memory client cache before retrying (same as the existing fix). ## Behavior `acompletion()` will retry at most once (`max_retries = 2`) when: 1. The exception chain indicates the underlying httpx client was closed (`reason=closed_http_client`). 2. The call is identified as Azure and the exception chain indicates an API connection error (`reason=azure_api_connection_error`). ## Risks ### High 1. Over-broad retry trigger via string matching in `_has_api_connection_error()`. This can false-positive on unrelated failures that contain similar text and cause a retry + cache flush. 2. Global cache flush amplification. Flushing `in_memory_llm_clients_cache` can affect concurrent requests for other providers/models and increase latency under transient Azure incidents. ### Medium 1. Azure detection gaps. Azure behind APIM/proxies/custom domains/national clouds may not match `azure/` or `.openai.azure.com`, so the Azure-specific retry may not trigger in those deployments. 2. Exception-chain traversal is single-branch (`__cause__ or __context__`). In rare cases, detection may miss a relevant nested exception, reducing retry reliability. ---

### Motivation
- Requests to `/admin/expedition-types` were failing because MVC could not find `Index`/`Upsert` views for the `ExpeditionTypesPageController`, causing runtime `InvalidOperationException` when rendering the admin page. 
- Providing the expected Razor files under the `ExpeditionTypesPage` view folder restores normal view discovery and prevents the error.

### Description
- Added `src/Web/Areas/Admin/Views/ExpeditionTypesPage/Index.cshtml` using the same list markup as the existing Expedition Types index view. 
- Added `src/Web/Areas/Admin/Views/ExpeditionTypesPage/Upsert.cshtml` to support create/edit actions that return `View("Upsert", ...)` and reused the existing form markup. 
- Committed both files so the `ExpeditionTypesPageController` can resolve its views without changing controller logic.

### Testing
- Attempted to run `dotnet build TravelCleanArch.sln`, but `dotnet` is not installed in this environment so the build could not be executed (failed). 
- Attempted a Playwright navigation and screenshot of `http://localhost:7251/admin/expedition-types`, but the request returned `ERR_EMPTY_RESPONSE` so the UI could not be validated end-to-end (failed).

author: qaid
body:
## Summary

Migrates toggle hotkey storage from `UserDefaults` to file-based storage in Application Support. Custom hotkey shortcuts now persist across app reinstalls and uninstalls, matching the proven pattern already used by the vocabulary feature.

- Stores hotkey in `~/Library/Application Support/LookMaNoHands/toggleHotkey.json`
- Automatic backward compatibility migration from UserDefaults
- Atomic file writes prevent corruption
- Comprehensive logging with emoji prefixes for debugging

## Testing

All 7 tests from the implementation plan should pass:
- Fresh install defaults to Cmd+Shift+D
- Custom hotkey persists within same session
- Custom hotkey persists across reinstalls ✨
- UserDefaults migration works correctly
- Reset to defaults works
- Nil handling cleans up files
- File corruption is handled gracefully

author: janjakes
body:
## Motivation for the change, related issues
This PR improves the way `defineWpConfigConstants` rewrites `wp-config.php`.

Extracted from #2539 without the auto-configure feature and CLI changes, this only improves the current behavior by introducing a new `WP_Config_Transformer` class.

The previous approach to modifying `wp-config.php` (`rewrite-wp-config-to-define-constants.php`) was a single monolithic function that handled both reading and rewriting constants in a single pass, with the token array reversed and manipulated through output buffer concatenation. It was hard to follow, extend, and test.

This PR replaces it with a `WP_Config_Transformer` class — a token-based service with clear, composable methods for inspecting and modifying the configuration.

This also adds the following improvements and simplifications:
- New constants are injected at a more appropriate location in `wp-config.php` (before the "stop editing" comment, ABSPATH definition, or `wp-settings.php` require) instead of being prepended at the top of the file in a `<?php ... ?>` block.
- Removed handling of expression-based constant names (e.g. `define('SITE'.'_URL', ...)`), which wrapped them in `if(!defined())` guards. This was an edge case that doesn't occur in real-world `wp-config.php` files.
- Removed the `whenAlreadyDefined` parameter from `defineWpConfigConstants` — it always rewrites now. The only caller that used `'skip'` mode was `ensureWpConfig`, which now handles that logic directly via `constant_exists()`.

Related: #2539, #2530

## Implementation details

- **New `WP_Config_Transformer` PHP class** (`wp-config-transformer.php`) with methods to check, define, and update constants, and smart anchor detection for inserting new definitions (before the "stop editing" comment, ABSPATH definition, or `wp-settings.php` require).
- **Rewritten `defineWpConfigConstants`** — delegates to `WP_Config_Transformer.define_constants()`, removing the `'rewrite'`/`'skip'` mode parameter.
- **File renaming** — `rewrite-wp-config.ts` → `wp-config.ts`, old PHP script deleted.

## Testing Instructions (or ideally a Blueprint)

Run the transformer and wp-config tests:
```bash
cd packages/playground/wordpress && npx vitest run src/test/wp-config-transformer.spec.ts
cd packages/playground/wordpress && npx vitest run src/test/wp-config.spec.ts
```

Test the `defineWpConfigConsts` Blueprint step manually:
1. Start the dev server: `npx nx dev playground-website`
2. Open [this Blueprint](http://127.0.0.1:5400/website-server/#{"steps":[{"step":"defineWpConfigConsts","consts":{"WP_DEBUG":true,"MY_CONST":"hello"},"method":"rewrite-wp-config"}]})
3. Verify the constants were added in `wp-config.php` via the File Browser.

author: andytwf
body:
## Summary
This change adds support for an optional `userClaim` field across multiple chat entities (Messages, Reactions, Presence Members, and Typing Events). The `userClaim` field is a server-provided string extracted from JWT claims embedded in realtime message extras, enabling better user identification and authentication tracking in chat operations.

[CHA-1243]

## Key Changes

- **Messages**: Added `userClaim` field to Message objects with specification requirements that it is read-only, server-provided, and extracted from JWT claims in realtime message extras or REST API responses.

- **Message Reactions**: Added `userClaim` field support to both raw message reaction events (`MessageReactionRawEvent`) and ephemeral room reactions (`Reaction`), with the same read-only, server-provided semantics.

- **Presence Members**: Added `userClaim` field to `PresenceMember` objects and presence events, extracted from the underlying Ably realtime presence message extras.

- **Typing Events**: Added `userClaim` field to typing event changes with an additional requirement that the claim must be preserved across heartbeat events and inactivity timeouts for a given `clientId`.

## Implementation Details

- All `userClaim` fields are marked as optional and read-only
- Clients cannot send `userClaim` when publishing messages, reactions, or entering presence
- The field is consistently extracted from `extras.userClaim` in the underlying Ably realtime messages
- For REST API responses, the field is extracted from response data if present
- All changes include corresponding testable specification points (CHA-M2h, CHA-MR7a1, CHA-ER2a, CHA-PR6a1, CHA-T13a1)
- Updated data structure examples in the specification to show the new optional field

author: meatuses
body: ## Description Remove `kube-apiserver-healthcheck` proxy sidecar for kube-apiserver, enable anonymous access to `/healthz`, `/livez`, `/readyz` endpoints via `AuthenticationConfiguration`. Now, health endpoints could be requested directly from apiserver port, and verbose output is available via `?verbose` query. Support in kube 1.31 is enabled via feature flag `AnonymousAuthConfigurableEndpoints` Additionally, these paths are now explicitly forbidden in publish API ingress `kubernetes-api`. **CIS Benchmark (kube-bench)** throws a warning when `anonymous-auth=false` is not set, but this parameter [is not compatible](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/#anonymous-authenticator-configuration) with `AuthenticationConfiguration.anonymous`. Our configuration only allows access to probe endpoints, so the warning is not relevant. ``` [WARN] 1.2.1 Ensure that the --anonymous-auth argument is set to false (Manual) 1.2.1 Edit the API server pod specification file /etc/kubernetes/manifests/kube-apiserver.yaml on the control plane node and set the below parameter. --anonymous-auth=false ``` **Comparison in resource consumption below.** Measurements taken with synthetic load requesting `/healthz` endpoint through healthcheck proxy (port 3990) and directly from apiserver port (port 6443), separately. - **healthcheck** container takes up a lot of additional memory (**1GiB**), while **apiserver** by itself only takes up small amount of additional memory (**150MiB**) while serving these requests. - **healtcheck** container may use up to **3.5 additional cores** cores while proxying. - **kube-apiserver** may serve much more of these requests directly (**9.47K req/s** vs **1.84 req/s** in this measurement) ## Why do we need it, and what problem does it solve? Since anonymous access could be granularly enabled with [AnonymousAuthConfigurableEndpoints](https://kubernetes.io/docs/reference/access-authn-authz/authentication/#anonymous-authenticator-configuration) feature, we could remove separate healthcheck proxy. Also, there is performance and resources concern. ## Why do we need it in the patch release (if we do)? ## Checklist - [ ] The code is covered by unit tests. - [ ] e2e tests passed. - [ ] Documentation updated according to the changes. - [x] Changes were tested in the Kubernetes cluster manually. ## Changelog entries ```changes section: control-plane-manager type: feature summary: Anonymous access to kube-apiserver health endpoints is now enabled via AuthenticationConfiguration and proxy sidecar is removed. impact: Kube-apiserver will be restarted due to changes in manifest. impact_level: default ```

body:
Pillow 12.1.1 removes APIs deprecated since v3.0 and v10.0.0. Two breaking changes required code updates:

**Changes:**
- `swmmio/graphics/utils.py`: `Image.LANCZOS` → `Image.Resampling.LANCZOS` (removed in Pillow 11.0.0)
- `swmmio/vendor/images2gif.py`: `image.tostring()` / `np.fromstring()` → `image.tobytes()` / `np.frombuffer()` (deprecated since Pillow 3.0)

```python
# Before
img.thumbnail(size, Image.LANCZOS)
self.pixels = np.fromstring(image.tostring(), np.uint32)

# After  
img.thumbnail(size, Image.Resampling.LANCZOS)
self.pixels = np.frombuffer(image.tobytes(), np.uint32)
```

All graphics tests pass with Pillow 12.1.1.

RuleSet 定义是架构规范的生产代码，但错误地放置在测试项目中。此 PR 将其迁移到 Specification 类库，并重组测试文件。

## 变更内容

**文件迁移**
- 53 个 RuleSet 文件：`src/tests/ArchitectureTests/Specification/RuleSets/` → `src/tools/Specification/RuleSets/`
  - 43 个 `AdrxxxRuleSet.cs` 定义文件
  - 10 个 ADR907 辅助文件（策略模式实现）

**测试重组**
- 6 个测试文件：`RuleSets/ADRxxx/tests/` → `Tests/RuleSets/ADRxxx/`

**命名空间更新**
- RuleSet：`Zss.BilliardHall.Tests.ArchitectureTests.Specification.RuleSets.{ADR}` → `Zss.BilliardHall.Specification.RuleSets.{ADR}`
- 测试：`...RuleSets.{ADR}.tests` → `...Tests.RuleSets.{ADR}`

**其他**
- `Specification/GlobalUsings.cs`：添加 `System.Diagnostics`
- `ArchitectureTests/GlobalUsings.cs`：更新 ADR907 引用
- 修复 20 个文件的 UTF-8 BOM 编码

## 结构对比

**之前**
```
src/tests/ArchitectureTests/Specification/RuleSets/
  ├── ADR001/Adr001RuleSet.cs + tests/
  ├── ...
  └── ADR990/
```

**之后**
```
src/tools/Specification/RuleSets/          # 生产代码

  └── ...

src/tests/ArchitectureTests/Specification/Tests/RuleSets/  # 测试代码
  ├── ADR001/
  └── ADR907/

## 优势

- **职责分离**：生产代码和测试代码物理隔离
- **可重用性**：RuleSet 可被其他项目引用（通过 RuleSetRegistry 反射自动发现）

✅ 707 个测试全部通过

body:
## Problem
Every tool in `src/.opencode/tool/` had identical copy-pasted `getFernUrl()` and `getAuthHeaders()` functions. This is a classic DRY violation affecting 12 files (14 lines × 12 = 168 lines of identical code).

## Solution
Created a shared utilities module at `src/.opencode/tool/utils.ts` that exports these helper functions, then refactored all tools to import from it.

## Changes
- **New file**: `src/.opencode/tool/utils.ts` (28 lines)
- **Refactored 12 tools** to import from utils instead of inline definitions:
  - Memory tools: delete, list, read, search, write
  - Scheduler tools: schedule, schedule-manage
  - Task tools: create, list, next, update
  - Channel tool: send-message

## Impact

## Skin Gifting Feature - Complete ✅

Successfully implemented a complete skin gifting system allowing users to purchase and gift cosmetic skins to other users using in-game currency.

### Implementation Checklist
- [x] Create skinShop data structure with all available skins
- [x] Add "Gift Skin" button to user profile page (visible only when viewing others' profiles)

  - [x] Show success feedback (toast, animation, sound)

  - [x] Added proper rollback notification on failure
  - [x] Moved notifications/logs to success callback only
- [x] Code review completed and issues addressed
- [x] Security considerations reviewed

### Key Features
✅ **Transaction Safety**: Uses Firebase transactions for atomic operations  
✅ **Error Handling**: Comprehensive error messages and recovery  
✅ **UI/UX**: Matches existing design with gold/orange gradient button  
✅ **Database Logging**: All gifts logged to `giftLogs` for record-keeping  
✅ **Notifications**: Recipients notified of received gifts  
✅ **Duplicate Prevention**: Skins already owned are marked as unavailable  

### Database Schema
- `users/{uid}/points` - Decremented for sender (atomic)
- `users/{uid}/ownedSkins` - Appended for recipient (atomic)  
- `notifications/{uid}` - Gift notification for recipient
- `giftLogs/{pushId}` - Permanent transaction record

### Files Changed
- **index.html**: +177 lines added

### Testing Notes
Since this is a Firebase-authenticated application, full integration testing requires:
1. Authentication to the live Firebase instance
2. Multiple user accounts to test gifting between users
3. Sufficient points balance to test transactions

The implementation follows existing patterns in the codebase and should work seamlessly with the live environment.

### Security Summary

✅ Input validation on all user actions  
✅ Firebase security rules apply to all database operations

<!-- START COPILOT ORIGINAL PROMPT -->



<details>

<summary>Original prompt</summary>

> ## Goal: Implement a Skin Gifting Feature
> 
> The goal is to allow a user (the sender) to purchase and gift a cosmetic skin to another user (the recipient) using their in-game currency (points).
> 
> ### 1. User Interface (UI) Changes
> 
> **A. Add "Gift Skin" Button to User Profile Page:**
> - In `index.html`, locate the `userProfilePage` container.
> - When a user is viewing *another user's* profile, a "Gift Skin" button should be visible. This button should be alongside or near the "Send Message" button. It should be hidden when viewing one's own profile.
> - The button should be styled similarly to other profile action buttons (e.g., `user-opt-btn`).
> - **Implementation:** Modify the `openUserProfile(uid)` function. When setting up the profile page, check if `uid === auth.currentUser.uid`. If not, create and display the "Gift Skin" button. Attach an `onclick` event to it, like `openGiftModal(uid)`.
> 
> **B. Create the Gifting Modal (`giftSkinModal`):**
> - Create a new modal in `index.html` that is hidden by default. It should have a backdrop and a main content area.
> - The modal should have a title like "Gift a Skin to [Recipient's Name]".
> - It will contain a list (`giftableSkinsList`) where available skins for gifting will be rendered.
> - **Styling:** Style it similarly to the `shopModal` or `reactionViewerModal` for a consistent look.
> 
> ### 2. Gifting Logic (JavaScript Functions)
> 
> **A. `openGiftModal(recipientId)` function:**
> - This function is called when the "Gift Skin" button is clicked.
> - It should first fetch the recipient's data, specifically their `ownedSkins`.
> - It will then display the `giftSkinModal`.
> - It will dynamically render the list of giftable skins by iterating through the global `skinShop` object.
> - For each skin in the shop, it should create a list item showing the skin's name, icon, and cost.
> - **Important:** It must *not* display skins that the recipient *already owns*. If `recipient.ownedSkins.includes(skin.id)`, that skin should be grayed out, marked as "Already Owned", and made unclickable.
> - Each clickable skin item should have an `onclick` event that calls `confirmSkinGift(recipientId, skin.id)`.
> 
> **B. `confirmSkinGift(recipientId, skinId)` function:**
> - This function is called when the sender selects a skin from the gift modal.
> - It should retrieve the skin's details (especially `cost`) from the `skinShop` object.
> - It must check if the sender (`userData.points`) has enough points to cover the `cost`.
>   - If not, show a toast: `"Insufficient Coins"`.
>   - If yes, call `showCustomConfirm` with a message like: `"Gift the ${skin.name} skin to ${recipientName} for ${skin.cost} Coins?"`. The `onYes` callback will be `() => executeSkinGift(recipientId, skinId)`.
> 
> **C. `executeSkinGift(recipientId, skinId)` function:**
> - This is the core transaction function.
> - **1. Deduct Points:** Subtract the skin's `cost` from the sender's points. Use a Firebase transaction for safety: `db.ref('users/' + auth.currentUser.uid + '/points').transaction(...)`.
> - **2. Add Skin to Recipient:** Add the `skinId` to the recipient's `ownedSkins` array. This should also use a Firebase transaction to safely append to the array.
> - **3. Create Notification:** Push a new notification to the recipient's notification feed: `db.ref('notifications/' + recipientId).push(...)`. The message should be something like `"${senderName} gifted you the ${skin.name} skin!"`. Include a `type: 'gift'` and the sender's UID.
> - **4. Log the Transaction:** Create a new root-level path `giftLogs` for record-keeping. Push a new entry: `db.ref('giftLogs').push({ from: senderId, to: recipientId, skinId: skinId, cost: cost, timestamp: firebase.database.ServerValue.TIMESTAMP })`.
> - **5. UI Feedback:**
>   - Close the gift modal.
>   - Show a success toast: `"Gift sent successfully!"`.
>   - Optionally, trigger a visual effect like `spawnFlyingCoins()` to make it feel rewarding.
> 
> ### 3. Database Schema Impact
> 
> - **`users/{uid}/points`**: Decremented for the sender.
> - **`users/{uid}/ownedSkins`**: Array is appended for the recipient.
> - **`notifications/{uid}`**: A new gift notification is added for the recipient.
> - **`giftLogs/{pushId}`**: A new path to store a permanent record of all gift transactions.
> 
> ### Files to Modify
> 
> - **`index.html`**:
>   - Add the HTML structure for the new `giftSkinModal`.
>   - Add the new JavaScript functions (`openGiftModal`, `confirmSkinGift`, `executeSkinGift`).
>   - Modify `openUserProfile` to include the "Gift Skin" button logic.

body:
Provides Japanese language explanation for the overflow protection added to `Prime::sieve` in PR #8, as requested in review comment.

The original concern: on 32-bit targets, `limit == u32::MAX` causes `n + 1` to overflow when allocating `vec![true; n + 1]`, leading to wraparound and panic.

**Changes:**
- No code changes required - the overflow protection using `checked_add(1)` was already implemented in the previous commit
- This PR exists solely to provide the requested Japanese explanation for that change

**説明 (Explanation in Japanese):**

`Prime::sieve`メソッドでは、素数判定用の配列を確保する際に`vec![true; n + 1]`を使用しています。32ビット環境で`limit`が`u32::MAX`の場合、`n + 1`の計算でオーバーフローが発生し、配列サイズの計算が不正確になる問題がありました。

これを防ぐため、`checked_add(1)`を使用してオーバーフローを検出し、オーバーフロー時には明確なエラーメッセージでパニックするように修正されています。

```rust
let size = n.checked_add(1).expect("Prime::sieve: limit too large (n + 1 overflows usize)");
let mut is_prime = vec![true; size];
```

body:
Title
feat: bootstrap backend with configuration, middleware, and utilities

Summary
This PR sets up the backend service with a validated environment configuration, core middleware stack, request/response utilities, and MongoDB connectivity. It also adds foundational error handling and logging to support building API features safely and consistently.

Changes

- Add environment configuration and validation:
- Define environment schema using Zod.
- Introduce an example .env configuration file to document required variables.
- Implement logging and HTTP request monitoring:
- Add a Winston-based logger with custom formatting and transports.
- Integrate a morgan logger utility that forwards HTTP logs to the custom logger.
- Add core Express setup and middleware:
- Initialize the Express app with JSON/urlencoded parsing.
- Add CORS utility and middleware for cross-origin request handling.
- Add rate limiter middleware for basic request throttling.
- Add async handler middleware for wrapping async route controllers.
- Standardize responses and validation:
- Implement a success response utility for consistent API responses.
- Add a validation utility with error formatting and handling for request payloads.
- Improve error handling:
- Introduce an APIError class for structured errors.
- Implement a global error handler middleware for centralized error processing.
- Add TypeScript types for Express requests and error handling.
- Add routes and health checks:
- Implement main and health check routes wired to the success response utility.
- Infrastructure and tooling:
- Add MongoDB connection utility with error handling.
- Add backend TypeScript configuration.
- Update frontend .gitignore to align with the new backend setup.

author: veeceey
body:
Fixes #5714

## Problem

`z.record()` uses `Reflect.ownKeys()` to iterate over input properties, which includes non-enumerable properties. This causes `z.json()` and `z.record()` to reject objects that have non-enumerable properties like the `~standard` property added by `z.toJSONSchema()` since v4.2.0.

For example:
```ts
const schema = z.object({ name: z.string() });
const jsonSchema = z.toJSONSchema(schema);

z.json().safeParse(jsonSchema).success; // false -- should be true
```

The `~standard` property is non-enumerable and contains functions, so when `z.record(z.string(), z.json())` (used internally by `z.json()`) encounters it, it tries to validate function values against the json schema and fails.

## Fix

Added a `propertyIsEnumerable` check in the record validation loop to skip non-enumerable properties. This aligns `z.record()` with `z.object()`, which already uses `for...in` (enumerable-only iteration).

The fix preserves Symbol key support (via `Reflect.ownKeys`) while filtering out non-enumerable properties that shouldn't participate in validation.

## Tests

Added three tests:
- Record skips non-enumerable properties during validation
- Record still validates enumerable properties correctly
- `z.json()` accepts objects with non-enumerable `~standard` properties

All existing tests pass (3580 tests).

body:
The recent template sync introduced stricter ruff linting rules via `.pre-commit-config.yaml`, causing `make fmt` to fail with 66 violations.

## Changes

**Combined nested `with` statements (SIM117)**
- Converted 56 instances to modern Python 3.10+ multi-context syntax
- Example:
  ```python
  # Before
  with patch("rhiza_tools.commands.release.run_git_command", side_effect=mock_git):
      with patch("typer.confirm", return_value=False):
          release_command()
  
  # After
  with (
      patch("rhiza_tools.commands.release.run_git_command", side_effect=mock_git),
      patch("typer.confirm", return_value=False),
  ):
      release_command()
  ```

**Fixed pytest.raises violations (PT012)**
- Moved 10 `assert` statements outside `pytest.raises()` contexts to comply with single-statement rule

**Suppressed intentional security warnings**
- Added `# noqa: S603, S607, S110` for subprocess calls and exception handling already marked safe with `# nosec`

**Simplified exception handling (SIM105)**
- Replaced `try-except-pass` with `contextlib.suppress(SystemExit)` in test module initialization

body:
### Motivation
- Provide a more capable, resilient video playback path for Tizen by routing files through a single player that can use native playback or fall back to HLS/DASH/FLV engines when needed.
- Improve format coverage so remote/live/HLS/DASH/FLV streams and additional containers are routed into appropriate players instead of failing silently.

### Description
- Added a new `CustomTizenVideoPlayer` class that centralizes playback and selects strategy by file extension, with on-demand runtime loading for `hls.js`, `dash.js`, and `flv.js` and a native fallback using the page `video` element.
- Integrated the custom player into `TysonPlayer` initialization (`this.customVideoPlayer`), player-back navigation cleanup, and replaced the old direct `video.src` path with an `async` `playVideo` that routes through `customVideoPlayer` and shows graceful error UI on failure.
- Expanded recognized video extensions in `supportedVideoFormats` to include `.avi`, `.m3u8`, `.ts`, `.m2ts`, and `.mpd` so more files are detected and handled by the correct engine.
- Improved thumbnail and rendering flow by batching render chunks, adding a thumbnail queue with concurrency limits, and safer thumbnail loading with timeouts to avoid blocking UI.

### Testing
- Ran static syntax check `node --check js/main.js`, which completed successfully.

author: silverwind
body:
- Replace the e2e tests initialization with a simple bash script, removing the previous Go harness.
- `make test-e2e` is the single entry point. It always starts a fully isolated ephemeral Gitea instance with its own temp directory, SQLite database, and config — no interference with the developer's running instance.
- A separate `gitea-e2e` binary is built via `EXECUTABLE_E2E` using `TEST_TAGS` (auto-includes sqlite with `CGO_ENABLED=1`), keeping the developer's regular `gitea` binary untouched.
- No more split into database-specific e2e tests. Test timeouts are strict, can be relaxed later if needed.
- Simplified and streamlined the playwright config and test files.
- Remove all output generation of playwright and all references to visual testing.
- Tests run on Chrome locally, Chrome + Firefox on CI.
- Simplified CI workflow — visible separate steps for frontend, backend, and test execution.
- All exported env vars use `GITEA_TEST_E2E_*` prefix.
- Use `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS` to pass flags to playwright, e.g. `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS="--ui" make test-e2e` for UI mode or `GITEA_TEST_E2E_FLAGS="--headed" make test-e2e` for headed mode.
- Use `GITEA_TEST_E2E_DEBUG=1 make test-e2e` to show Gitea server output.

### 2. Typography & Spacing Enforcement
- Enforced body size 16-18px and line-height 1.6-1.8 globally
- Updated spacing throughout to use `sp-1` through `sp-5` scale (8/16/24/40/64px)
- Added `max-w-prose` (720px) constraint for narrative text blocks
- Created `.ui-text` class for reduced line-height UI elements

### 3. Component Rules Alignment
- **Button** (`button.tsx`): Updated transitions to `duration-kn-base`, standardized hover states (90% opacity), added comments for variants
- **Input** (`input.tsx`): Updated transitions to use design system tokens
- **Card** (`card.tsx`): Updated spacing to use `sp-*` scale, added `font-heading` to CardTitle
- **Badge** (`badge.tsx`): Updated transitions, added `muted` variant, standardized hover states
- **Dialog** (`dialog.tsx`): Updated padding and spacing to use `sp-*` scale, improved transitions

### 4. Global Layout Structure

- Added `kn` color namespace for direct access to core palette

- **No new features or routes added** - pure design system implementation

author: veeceey
body:
##### SUMMARY

The SSH connection plugin's `control_path_dir` option has a hardcoded default of `~/.ansible/cp`, which ignores the `ANSIBLE_HOME` configuration setting entirely. When a user configures `ANSIBLE_HOME` to a custom path (e.g. `~/.cache/ansible`), the control path directory still gets created under `~/.ansible/cp`.

This removes the hardcoded default and adds a runtime fallback to `$ANSIBLE_HOME/cp` when no explicit `control_path_dir` is configured. This is consistent with how other path defaults in the codebase reference `ANSIBLE_HOME`.

An earlier PR (#82026) addressed this but was closed with a reference to #76114, which only added the `ANSIBLE_HOME` config option itself without updating the SSH plugin's default. Confirmed still broken on 2.17.4 per the issue thread.

Fixes #79737

##### ISSUE TYPE

- Bugfix Pull Request

##### COMPONENT NAME

ssh connection plugin

##### ADDITIONAL INFORMATION

Tested by verifying:
- When `ANSIBLE_HOME` is set to a custom path, `control_path_dir` now defaults to `$ANSIBLE_HOME/cp`
- When `control_path_dir` is explicitly configured, the explicit value is still used
- Added unit test covering the fallback behavior

## Summary

- ワークフローノードの Handle を縦配置（Top/Bottom）から横配置（Left/Right）に変更
- これにより、ワークフローの視覚的な流れが「左→右」に統一され、より直感的なレイアウトになる
- Blueprint ノードの展開レイアウトも横方向に対応

## Changes

- **14個のノードコンポーネント**: Handle position を `Position.Top/Bottom` から `Position.Left/Right` に変更
  - SendMessageNode, CreateChannelNode, ShuffleAssignNode, SetGameFlagNode, DeleteChannelNode, CreateRoleNode, BlueprintNode, ChangeChannelPermissionNode, CreateCategoryNode, AddRoleToRoleMembersNode, SelectBranchNode, DeleteCategoryNode, DeleteRoleNode, ConditionalBranchNode
- **Blueprint 展開ロジック**: 縦方向レイアウト（Y軸）から横方向レイアウト（X軸）に変更
  - `currentY` → `currentX`
  - `VERTICAL_SPACING (200)` → `HORIZONTAL_SPACING (350)`
- **ドキュメント更新**: `node-system-architecture.md` と `node-creator` スキルのテンプレートを更新

author: ifiokjr
body:
## Summary

- Replace all Homebrew infrastructure (nix-homebrew, homebrew-core/cask/bundle inputs) with [nix-casks](https://github.com/atahanyorganci/nix-casks) which converts Homebrew cask definitions into pure Nix derivations
- Move 38 GUI apps to `environment.systemPackages` via nix-casks — apps are downloaded directly via `fetchurl` with no Homebrew process, significantly speeding up `darwin-rebuild`
- Enable `mkalias` activation script to create `/Applications/Nix Apps/` aliases (Spotlight/Launchpad visibility)
- Add font packages (`google-fonts`, `inconsolata`, `recursive`, `roboto`) to `home.nix` to replace Homebrew font casks
- Remove all Homebrew references from hooks, CI, shell aliases, and documentation

**6 apps dropped** (not available in nix-casks): `google-chrome`, `google-drive`, `gpg-suite`, `nordvpn`, `steam`, `zoom` — install manually if needed.

**BREAKING CHANGE**: Homebrew is no longer managed by nix-darwin. After applying, optionally uninstall Homebrew to reclaim disk space.

## Test plan

- [ ] Verify `dprint check` passes
- [ ] Verify `shellcheck` passes on all bash scripts
- [ ] Verify `nix flake check` passes (with `--impure --no-build`)
- [ ] Run `rebuild` to apply via darwin-rebuild
- [ ] Verify apps appear in `/Applications/Nix Apps/`
- [ ] Verify Spotlight can find nix-installed apps
- [ ] Verify CI passes on both macOS and Ubuntu

author: misialq
body:
This change introduces a new tool, `find_path`, to the Rachis MCP server. This tool allows researchers to discover potential analysis pipelines by finding a sequence of actions that can transform a given starting semantic type (e.g., `SampleData[SequencesWithQuality]`) into a target semantic type (e.g., `FeatureTable[Frequency]`). The implementation uses a Breadth-First Search (BFS) algorithm within the `KnowledgeGraph` class to ensure the shortest path is found, while handling circular dependencies and property compatibility correctly. Additionally, a minor fix was applied to `tsconfig.json` to resolve type checking errors.

author: jose-compu
body:
## Summary

Replaces the Solc AST-based `Flattener` in `forge flatten` with the Solar-based
`ProjectPathsConfig::flatten` path. The previous implementation compiled the
project via Solc solely to obtain ASTs for flattening. The replacement resolves
imports through the dependency graph using Solar-based parsing, removing the
need for Solc compilation during flattening.

Closes #10965

## Changes

- `crates/common/src/utils.rs`: Remove `Flattener`, `FlattenerError`,
  `SolcError`, and `SolcLanguage` imports. Simplify `flatten()` to use
  `ProjectPathsConfig::flatten` directly.
- `crates/forge/tests/cli/flatten.rs`: New test module with 4 integration
  tests.
- `crates/forge/tests/cli/main.rs`: Register the new `flatten` test module.

## Tests

Added integration tests covering:
- Single file flattening (no imports)
- Multi-file flattening with import resolution and dependency ordering
- File output via `--output` flag
- Flattening without Solc compilation artifacts

author: mic92
body:
The dist object in npm packuments contains fields that can change after a package is published, causing hash mismatches in fixed-output derivations:

  - signatures: changes when npm rotates registry signing keys (old key SHA256:jl3bwswu80Pjj... expired 2025-01-29)
  - npm-signature: legacy format being progressively removed
  - attestations: provenance metadata added post-publication

Only keep the three fields npm actually needs during install: tarball, integrity, and shasum. Also strip the informational-only fileCount and unpackedSize fields.

This is the same approach already used for top-level and version-level field whitelisting.

Ref: https://github.com/numtide/llm-agents.nix/issues/2459

author: copilot
body:
Recording countdown was forcing playback to start from beat 0 by temporarily overriding `global_loop_start`, ignoring the user's loop configuration.

## Changes

- **`countdown_tick` method**: Removed temporary override of `global_loop_start` that forced recording to start at beat 0
  - Deleted: 5 lines that saved, set to 0, and restored `global_loop_start` and `gloop_start` 
  - Retained: `sync_start()` and `begin_actual_recording()` calls, which already respect `global_loop_start`

Recording now starts at the user-configured loop point. The `sync_start()` method calculates the correct audio offset and beat position based on `global_loop_start`.

```python
# Before: forced to beat 0
old_loop_start = self.global_loop_start
self.global_loop_start = 0
self.gloop_start.set(0)
self.sync_start()  # starts at beat 0
self.global_loop_start = old_loop_start
self.gloop_start.set(old_loop_start)

# After: respects user setting
self.sync_start()  # starts at global_loop_start
```

author: veeceey
body:
Fixes #11259

When the compress middleware is active and the backend response already includes `Vary: Accept-Encoding`, the header gets duplicated in the response:

```
Vary: Accept-Encoding
Vary: Accept-Encoding
```

This happens for all three compression algorithms (gzip, brotli, zstd), since both the middleware and the backend independently add the header.

### Root Cause

**For brotli/zstd:** `CompressionHandler.ServeHTTP` unconditionally calls `rw.Header().Add("Vary", "Accept-Encoding")` before the backend handler runs. When the backend also sets the header, the result is a duplicate.

**For gzip:** The `klauspost/compress` gzhttp library [unconditionally adds](https://github.com/klauspost/compress/blob/master/gzhttp/compress.go#L483) `Vary: Accept-Encoding` as well.

### Fix

**For brotli/zstd:** Removed the upfront `Vary` header addition from `ServeHTTP` and moved it into the `responseWriter`. A new `ensureVaryHeader()` method checks if the header is already present before adding it, and is called at each point where headers are sent to the client.

**For gzip:** Wrapped the `ResponseWriter` passed to the gzhttp handler with a `deduplicateVaryWriter` that deduplicates `Vary` header values before they are sent. This avoids the duplicate without modifying the upstream library.

Added tests for all three encodings to verify no duplicate `Vary` headers when the backend already sets them.

body:
This pull request adds support for configuring MCP servers that communicate over stdio in addition to existing HTTP and SSE transports. It introduces new types, validation logic, and UI elements for handling stdio-based MCP servers, allowing users to specify command, arguments, working directory, and environment variables. The changes ensure robust validation, deduplication, and user feedback for these new server types.

**MCP stdio server support:**

* Added `stdio` as a valid `McpTransport`, and introduced new config types (`ClientMcpStdioServerConfig`, `McpStdioServerConfig`) to represent stdio-based servers, including fields for `command`, `args`, `cwd`, and `env` [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-74593bba02b62abe808396e31eb8ce9f501c8d00aecc5db15de78bc22e7abe87L23-R38) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d4d02e1e213a6e908bde87dfb239e6d84dfbaeed2616b5695726416fbb2b2acbL6-R28).
* Implemented parsing and validation logic for stdio server arguments and environment variables, including limits on the number of args and env vars, and key format validation [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-74593bba02b62abe808396e31eb8ce9f501c8d00aecc5db15de78bc22e7abe87R47-R49) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-74593bba02b62abe808396e31eb8ce9f501c8d00aecc5db15de78bc22e7abe87R463-R541) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d4d02e1e213a6e908bde87dfb239e6d84dfbaeed2616b5695726416fbb2b2acbR613) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d4d02e1e213a6e908bde87dfb239e6d84dfbaeed2616b5695726416fbb2b2acbR656-R741).
* Updated server deduplication logic to account for stdio server uniqueness based on command, args, cwd, and env [[1]](diffhunk://#diff-74593bba02b62abe808396e31eb8ce9f501c8d00aecc5db15de78bc22e7abe87R342-R401) [[2]](diffhunk://#diff-d4d02e1e213a6e908bde87dfb239e6d84dfbaeed2616b5695726416fbb2b2acbR211-R276) [[3]](diffhunk://#diff-d4d02e1e213a6e908bde87dfb239e6d84dfbaeed2616b5695726416fbb2b2acbL210-R312) [[4]](diffhunk://#diff-d4d02e1e213a6e908bde87dfb239e6d84dfbaeed2616b5695726416fbb2b2acbR656-R741).

author: veeceey
body:
Fixes #17207 CSS attribute selectors for HTML enumerated attributes (like `method`, `type`, `dir`, etc.) are supposed to match case-insensitively per the HTML spec. Browsers handle this correctly — `form[method="get"]` matches `
`. But Svelte's CSS pruning was doing a strict case-sensitive comparison, which meant: 1. The selector got incorrectly flagged as unused (no `css_unused_selector` warning was shown when spreads were involved, but the selector was still pruned) 2. The scoping class wasn't applied to the matching element 3. Styles silently disappeared in production builds The fix adds a set of known HTML attributes with case-insensitive enumerated values (sourced from the HTML spec) and uses it during CSS attribute selector matching. The explicit CSS `s` flag still overrides this behavior, as expected. ### Before ```svelte

Hello

``` ### After The selector correctly matches and styles are applied. ### Test plan - Added `attribute-selector-html-case-insensitive` CSS test covering `form[method]` and `input[type]` cases - All 179 existing CSS tests pass - Verified the existing `attribute-selector-case-sensitive` test (using `s` flag) still works correctly - Compiler error tests and validator tests all pass

author: turdjali
body:
### Motivation
- Prevent dynamic camera handoffs during shots so gameplay keeps a stable orbit/broadcast framing and stops following the cue ball. 
- Make cue strikes softer to improve mobile play pacing by reducing launch power. 
- Improve the rail overhead broadcast framing and make the break-dice UI sit lower on portrait screens for better visual balance.

### Description
- Added a global toggle `ENABLE_DYNAMIC_SHOT_CAMERAS = false` and gated creation of `actionView` and early pocket views so the system will not switch into cue-follow/pocket camera views during shots, keeping the orbit/broadcast camera fixed. 
- Reduced effective shot velocity by applying an extra `* 0.85` multiplier to `SHOT_BASE_SPEED`, lowering launch power by ~15%. 
- Tuned rail-overhead broadcast framing by changing `RAIL_OVERHEAD_DISTANCE_BIAS` from `1.05` to `1.02` to nudge the camera slightly closer, and increased `RAIL_OVERHEAD_AIM_PHI_LIFT` from `0.04` to `0.055` to tilt the view a bit more toward the cloth. 
- Adjusted portrait break-roll overlay positioning by adding `breakRollOverlayOffsetClass` and switching the break-dice container top padding to `pt-[30vh]` for portrait to move the text/frame and roll button downward.
- All changes are contained in `webapp/src/pages/Games/PoolRoyale.jsx`.

### Testing
- Ran the unit tests matching `test/poolRoyaleRules.test.ts` with `npm test -- --runInBand test/poolRoyaleRules.test.ts` and the suite passed (3 tests, 1 suite).
